title: Generic products manufactured under the brand's new drug application: the statement in the appendix to 105 CMR 720.000
subtopic: Products manufactured under the same NDA as the brand name product
rule_summary: The Introduction printed in Appendix A to 105 CMR 720.000, the Massachusetts List of Interchangeable Drugs at 105 CMR 720.200, states that several generic drug products are manufactured under the same new drug application (NDA) as the brand name drug products; that according to section 1.6 of the Orange Book, drug products with the same NDA are therapeutically equivalent; that Massachusetts regulations allow the interchange of these products; that distributors or repackagers of drug products manufactured under the same NDA as the brand name product are not identified in the Orange Book; that pharmacists who may not be able to determine if drug products are interchangeable should contact the manufacturers, distributors or repackagers; and that in addition the Department maintains an unofficial list of these products. The same appendix sets out a lookup in which a drug product whose same drug product, dosage form and strength has been assigned an 'A' rating by FDA in the Orange Book and is not listed on the Exception List is interchangeable, and a drug product not listed in the Orange Book is looked up by generic name on the Additional List, where the same drug product, dosage form and strength must be listed.
exam_relevance: Tests that a generic product manufactured under the same NDA as the brand name product is not excluded from interchange in Massachusetts merely because its distributor or repackager is not identified in the Orange Book, since the appendix to 105 CMR 720.000 states that Massachusetts regulations allow the interchange of these products.

authority.name: Massachusetts List of Interchangeable Drug Products, Appendix A
authority.section: 105 CMR 720.200, Appendix A, Introduction (paragraph on generic drug products manufactured under the same new drug application as the brand name drug products)

common_confusions: Concluding that a generic product manufactured under the brand's NDA cannot be interchanged because its distributor or repackager does not appear in the Orange Book. The appendix states that Massachusetts regulations allow the interchange of these products.

Treating the appendix lookup as the whole answer. The lookup covers Orange Book 'A' ratings, the Exception List and the Additional List, and the Introduction separately addresses products manufactured under the brand's NDA.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in 105 CMR 720.000 as published on mass.gov (the PDF linked from the regulation page dated 07/09/2004), in the Introduction in Appendix A at 105 CMR 720.200 (pages headed '720.220: continued') and in the appendix lookup steps.
